title: Emulator run-through of Wayne's session (Android, local test server)
body:
Ran on the Android emulator against a local server on a **Neon branch** (a copy of the database; test account, three seeded runs; background jobs and email off). Simulated GPS at ~5:00/km.

**Worked:**
- The sheet suggested 4:45–4:55/km reps (≈ 1:54–1:58 per 400 m) and 6:00–6:55/km easy.
- The − and + buttons and the per-rep time updated correctly.
- The run went warm-up → rep 1 at exactly 1:00 → "halfway, 210 metres to go" → recovery after 0.41 km → 30 s recovery → rep 2 → recovery → rep 3.
- The rep-pace cue fired.

**Found and fixed during the test:**
- "Set a pace" after "Coach on effort" brought back a generic 7:00–7:40/km instead of the suggestion.
- Nothing said which of −/+ is faster; there's now a hint line.
- "Your paces from last time you ran this session" was wrong: they only set it up, and it matches the rep shape, not the session. Reworded.
- The warm-up cue said "1 minutes". Fixed.

**Not verified:** the end of the session (emulator crashed in rep 3), and iOS (see the question about a debug server switch). Live pace showed 0:00 on the emulator; the simulated GPS has no speed, so this is probably not an app bug.

title: Code review: interval fix + Confirm session (8 findings, all fixed)
body:
A code review of the uncommitted changes found 2 important issues and 6 minor ones. All are fixed and both apps build.
- **Important:** on Android, the start-line idle credit took time off the run clock but not off the new phase timeline, so a timed phase could last minutes too long. The timeline now moves back with the clock (iOS already did this).
- **Important:** iOS and Android split some AI-plan phases differently (time vs distance). They now use the same rule.
- Walk-run got pace targets despite "no pace pressure". Fixed: no pace for run segments.
- A single configured rep announced the whole session summary as its cue. It now says "Each rep: 400 m, hard but controlled".
- Continuous plan phases lost their minutes-left context for the coach. Restored.
- The confirm sheet's date used UTC, so an NZ morning run showed as the previous day. It now uses the runner's time zone.
- Saved paces made the sheet wait for the server, and there was no way back to suggestions. Saved paces now show at once, with a "Use suggested paces" button.
- Two neighbouring phases with the same name weren't treated as a phase change. Fixed.

title: Confirm session: suggested paces before a configured session
body:
After configuring reps, a **Confirm session** sheet shows the session with target paces before it's prepared.
- **Where the paces come from:** the server works them out from the runner's best recent run (the same pace anchor the training plans use). Short reps are a little quicker than 5K pace, ~1 km reps are 5K pace, longer reps are 10K or threshold pace. Hill repeats are coached on effort. It isn't an AI call and costs no allowance.
- **Changing them:** − and + move a pace 5 s/km (− is faster). "Coach on effort instead" turns a pace off.
- **Memory:** if the runner changes a pace, it's remembered for that rep shape, with "Use suggested paces" to go back.
- **During the run:** the confirmed paces become the coach's targets, plus a cue when a rep is more than 10 s/km off the target. Walk-run never gets pace targets.
- **Not done yet:** watches don't get the targets.

title: Interval sessions skipped their reps — fixed
body:
**What happened:** Wayne's session (10 min warm-up, 4 × 400 m / 60 s, 5 min cool-down) went warm-up → "recover" → cool-down.

**Why:** both apps' phase timelines added time and distance separately from the start of the run. The 400 m reps were measured from 0 km, but he'd covered ~1.5 km in the warm-up, so they looked done already (Android). On iOS, distance reps had zero length. AI plan sessions mixing time and distance had the same bug: a timed warm-up made a tempo block end 1.5 km early.

**Fix:**
- Each phase now ends on its own measure, counted from where the runner actually entered it.
- A mixed session ends when its last phase does.
- Mixed sessions no longer get a made-up finish distance (it was putting Wayne in "final stretch" mode from the warm-up).
- Android checked heart-rate and pace triggers against the wrong phase's targets from rep 2 on. Fixed.
- iOS sessions without reps no longer guess timed phases at 0.1 km a minute.
- The halfway cue now works on distance reps ("210 metres to go").
- The live coach is now told the rep length and metres left.

title: Check the end of a configured session
body: In the emulator test the session ran correctly through warm-up → rep 1 → recovery → rep 2 → recovery → rep 3, then the emulator crashed. The last recovery, the cool-down announcement and the "session done" cue weren't seen on a device. The code path is the same one that already ends timed plans, but please listen for those three at the end of your next configured session.

title: Wayne's session on a real phone
body:
After the new builds and the redeploy:
- Setup → Run without route → Intervals → Configure session: **10 min warm-up, 4 × 400 m, 60 s recovery, 5 min cool-down**
- Tap Prepare: the **Confirm session** sheet should show your suggested paces (or say there aren't enough runs)
- Run it and check each rep is called in order, the halfway cue says metres left, the cool-down is announced after rep 4's recovery, and the session ends with a "session done" cue

Please write down anything that's late, missing or said twice.

title: Push and build the interval fix, Confirm session and rep strip?
body: You said to commit (done 2026-11-21, not pushed). Pushing the monorepo also auto-deploys Railway's test service. Next steps when you're ready: push both repos, build **Android 2.0.86 (128)** and **iOS 1.8.28 (99)**, and redeploy Replit (pace suggestions, the "metres left" coaching detail and this page).

title: Add a debug server switch to the iOS app for simulator testing?
body:
I could run the Android emulator against a local test server on a Neon branch (a copy of production, with background jobs off), so new server features could be tested before a redeploy. The iOS app can't do that: it has no debug server switch, and its network security settings block plain-HTTP connections to a local server.

Adding a **DEBUG-only** switch (Android has one: `debug_api_base_url`) plus an exception for local addresses would let me run the same tests on the iOS simulator. Release builds wouldn't change. OK to add?

title: Rep strip on the run screen
body:
You said yes (2026-11-21). Any session with a phase plan (configured reps, one-off AI sessions, plan workouts with more than one phase) now shows a strip under the coach panel:
- **REP 2 OF 4 · 210 m left** (or **RECOVERY 2 OF 4 · 0:35 left**, **WARM-UP · 6:12 left**), with a progress bar
- the target pace on reps, and **Next: Recovery 2 · 60 s** underneath
- red on reps, green on recoveries, warm-up and cool-down; **SESSION COMPLETE** at the end

It reads the same timeline the coach announces from, every second, so it keeps moving while the coach is talking or muted. Android `PhaseStrip` (RunSessionScreen.kt), iOS `PhaseStripView` (HomeScreens.swift).

Build-checked on both apps. Not yet seen on a screen: the emulator wouldn't boot again, so please check it during Wayne's session test.
